//: 'Split-mu' braking — left wheels on dry asphalt, right wheels on ice.
//1: Standard automotive validation test for ABS yaw stability.  Without
//2: individual-wheel ABS control, the asphalt-side wheels grip while
//3: the ice-side wheels lock — net result is a yawing moment that pulls
//4: the car toward the high-mu side.  Per-wheel ABS modulation lets
//5: each side use its own friction limit.
//7: Watch the yaw_rate column in the CSV.  BTCM-on should keep yaw
//8: near zero (car stays straight); BTCM-off should drift positive
//11: THE LAUNCH MUST NOT WRITE THE ANSWER.  The runway used to be 60 m,
//12: and the pre-boundary half of this scenario needs 130 m of it
//13: (78.4 m to reach 20 m/s, then 51.6 m of settle).  So the car
//14: straddled the seam at 40 mph under full throttle: the ice-side spun
//15: against the asphalt-side wheels (peak |slip| 0.71) and the car had
//16: already yawed 3.4 degrees before the brake event started — on the
//17: one test whose verdict IS the yaw.  The runway now covers the whole
//18: pre-brake half (see level/flat_split_mu.json for the distance
//19: budget): entry speed and a 2.60 s / 51.6 m settle both land on
//20: uniform asphalt, the car crosses onto the split coasting at
//21: 19.47 m/s and 0.37 deg of yaw, and settles a further 2.72 s /
//22: 52.2 m ON the split before the brake.  Measured yaw carried into
//23: the brake event: 1.37 deg, down from 3.41 deg, with yaw RATE at
//24: 0.00002 deg/s — the car is straight and no longer turning.  What
//25: remains is the one-off heading step the split's own coast-drag
//26: asymmetry produces in the first ~1.2 s on the surface, which is
//27: this test's physics rather than its launch.
//29: The brake application is unchanged — same full 1.0, same 13 s hold.
//30: Every event from the brake onward is shifted +3 s to sit after the
//33: THE COAST MUST NOT WALK OFF THE SEAM (2026-09-08).  That heading
//34: step was accepted as 'this test's physics' and nobody read pos_y.
//35: It is not the split's: the launch writes it (+0.40 deg by the
//36: throttle release — under full throttle the driven fronts do not
//37: spin equally, FL -0.089 / FR -0.094 slip — and the open-loop coast
//38: holds it, yaw rate 0.0000, for the 145 m to the brake).  0.4 deg
//39: over 145 m is 1.3 m; the EV1's front half-track is 0.735 m.
//40: Measured at the t=15 s brake
//41: event, this scenario file as of e3613d3, under the electricsim harness:
//42: pos_y +1.28 m / yaw +0.43 deg with the brake controller on the bus
//43: and +1.30 m / +0.43 deg without it — every wheel on asphalt, the
//44: two front slip traces mirror images (0.104 / 0.102 mean), a plain
//45: dry stop.  Other runs of the same scenario landed at +0.49 m and,
//46: spawned at y=-1.15 m, at +0.47 m: the drift is not a constant, it
//47: depends on the launch and on what else runs on the bus, so no
//48: spawn offset can place the car.  The scenario driver
//49: now HOLDS the lane instead: lane_hold engages a look-ahead COURSE
//50: controller on y=0 (the seam) for the whole coast, and lane_release
//51: on the brake tick centres the wheel so the stop itself is open-loop
//52: — what the car does under the brake is the brake system's answer,
//53: not the driver's.  Law + gains: Scenario::LaneHoldSteering.
//54: Measured with the hold (same harness, both legs): brake event at
//55: pos_y -0.028 m, course -0.03 deg, body yaw -0.87 deg (the crab a
//56: straight-running car carries on this surface, NOT a turn),
//57: wheel_mu 0.90/0.08 under FL/FR, steering 0.000, peak steering
//58: demand over the coast 0.04.  docs/abs_test_results.md has what the
//59: correctly placed car then does under the brake.
//62: left half asphalt 0.9, right half ice 0.08).
name: abs_split_mu

events.//1: that spins the drive wheels from a dead stop; see the PR

events.//1: across the asphalt settle, the crossing and the on-split settle.

events.//1: before set_brake in the sorted event list, so the stop is open-loop.
